transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I guess… things at home have been getting to me. My in-laws moved into our house, and since then I’ve been really keyed up and run down. I’m snapping at my wife, avoiding calls I’d normally take care of right away… and I almost let one of my musician’s contracts fall apart because I just couldn’t think straight.
Have you been feeling anxious or overwhelmed since your in-laws moved in?

Yeah… since they moved in, I’ve been pretty keyed up. Overwhelmed, I guess. I’m worn down, snapping at my wife, putting off calls I’d normally handle right away… and I almost messed up a musician’s contract because I couldn’t think straight.
Are you avoiding any specific activities or places because of your current situation?

Mostly calls, I guess. I’ve been avoiding work calls I’d normally handle right away. It’s not really a place… it’s just since my in-laws moved in, I get so keyed up and worn down that I put things off, and it’s started causing problems. I almost let a musician’s contract fall apart because I couldn’t think straight.
Have you been feeling sad or down since your in-laws moved in?
I don’t know… not sad exactly. Maybe just worn out. I haven’t really thought of it that way.
Are you avoiding calls because you fear something might happen or go wrong?

Not because I think something terrible will happen, exactly. It’s more… I’m so keyed up and worn down that I just don’t want to deal with them, and then I put them off. That’s what got me into trouble with that contract.
Have you been feeling sad or empty most of the day?
I’m not sure. I wouldn’t say empty most of the day… I just haven’t really been looking at it that way.
Do you find yourself worrying about things most days?
I’m not sure. I mean… I think about things a lot, but I don’t know if I’d call it worrying most days.
Do you often find yourself preoccupied with worries?
I don’t know… “preoccupied” feels a little strong. Things do stay on my mind, but I’m not sure I’d call it that.
Do you find yourself worrying about more things than just your current situation at home?
I’m not really sure. Mostly it feels tied to what’s going on at home… I haven’t thought much beyond that.
Do you often find yourself worrying about things even when there isn't a specific problem?
I don’t really know. I guess if there’s nothing specific going on, I’m not sure I’d call it worrying. My mind just kind of… goes there sometimes.
Do you worry about everyday things, like finances or health, even when there's no apparent problem?
Not really… I mean, I think about bills and health like anyone does, but I don’t know that I’m worrying about them when there’s no reason. It’s mostly when something brings it up.
Do you find yourself having thoughts that repeat over and over in your mind?
I don’t know… not in a way I’d call that, I guess. Some things stick in my head, but I haven’t really paid attention to whether it’s repeating over and over.
Do you find yourself doing things over and over that don't seem to have a reason?
Not that I’ve noticed. I mean, I have routines like anyone, but nothing that feels… unnecessary or like I have to keep doing it.
Do you feel compelled to perform specific rituals or behaviors to relieve anxiety?
No… I don’t think so. I don’t have any rituals like that, at least not that I’m aware of.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your sleep patterns since your in-laws moved in?
I’m not sure. I haven’t really been tracking it… maybe it’s a little different, but I couldn’t say for sure.
Have you experienced any significant distress or impairment in social or occupational areas of your life since your in-laws moved in?

Yeah… it has. Work’s been affected. I almost lost a musician’s contract recently, and my managing partner… he basically questioned whether I should still be handling big negotiations.

And at home, it’s gotten bad enough that my wife wanted us to get outside help. So… yes, I guess it’s been significant.
Do you find yourself worrying about things more days than not?
I don’t really know. I mean, I worry, sure… but I haven’t been keeping track of whether it’s most days or not.
Do you think your symptoms would improve if your in-laws were no longer living with you?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, that’s when all this started. Since they moved in, I’ve just been… keyed up, worn down. I’m snapping at my wife, putting off calls I’d normally take right away. I almost let a contract fall apart because I couldn’t think straight. So… yes, I’d hope it would improve.
Do you think your symptoms are directly caused by your in-laws moving in?

Yeah… I do. I mean, that’s when it started. Since they moved in, I’ve been keyed up all the time and just worn down. I’m snapping at my wife, dodging calls I’d normally handle, and I almost let a musician’s contract fall apart because I couldn’t think straight. So… yes, I think it’s connected.
